column2: The contractor's quote was so beautiful I almost framed it — then I saw the number.
The morning commute is a real bear, but you learn to bear it.
The kids picked up tennis this summer, so the whole house is now a racket in every sense.
The court asked for a full record of the night, so the DJ sent his latest record.
He proposed with a ring, then the ring went off mid-dinner and his mother took the call.
I told my son the rolls were fresh, then we watched one roll right off the table.
We sat at a round table while Dave bought the round — geometry and generosity finally agreeing.
The hotel said the room was perfectly safe, so naturally I locked my passport in the safe.
The circus seal sealed the contract with a clap.
Our cafe opened next to the tennis club, so on match days the servers serve and the players serve, and nobody knows who's eating.
She looked sharp at the wedding — the knife set wasn't the only sharp thing in the house.
The photographer yelled "shoot!" and my uncle ducked — he'd only ever heard it on a hunting trip.
Our vampire-hunting startup raised funding — the investors brought their own stakes, literally.
I told him to diversify his stock — he bought more chicken stock.
The mattress sprung in spring — the coil gave out just as the flowers came up.
I bit off more than I could chew at the buffet — literally, I had to spit out half a sandwich.
Our wedding budget broke the bank — and I'm not talking about the building's windows.
He brings home the bacon every night, which would be sweet if he didn't work at the pork plant.
I've been burning the candle at both ends this week — it's cheaper than two candles and twice as smoky.
We buried the hatchet years ago — the archaeologists will be so confused.
I tried to catch her eye across the bar, but she was wearing a goalie mask.
He quit smoking cold turkey — went straight from cigarettes to eating cold turkey.
When my aunt said "drop dead!" I just lay on the floor. She's very literal — it's a family trait.
The groom got cold feet at the altar — the church heating was off all winter.
My doctor told me to give jogging a shot, but I fainted at the sight of needles, so neither of us won.
She plays hard to get — mostly because she's terrible at hide and seek.
I put my foot in my mouth so often my dentist has my shoe size.
The weatherman rained on everyone's parade — literally, the forecast killed the Fourth of July.
I said "speak of the devil" and he took it as a summons — showed up in a cape.
I threw in the towel on the plumbing job — literally, it's clogging the drain.
My friend's pet crocodile is a gentle vegetarian — it only eats salad and other people's fingers.
Our hen lays square eggs — great for stacking, terrible for the carton.
The new resort offers cloud hammocks — solid clouds you can lie on, apparently.
I dropped the egg and it bounced — unbreakable eggs, breakfast is saved.
The farmer's honey tastes salty — turns out bears make terrible beekeepers.
My ice cream melted into soup — healthy, hot soup, according to the menu.
Our town's satellite fell out of orbit and landed in the lake — the TV's been grounded ever since.
The smoke detector stayed silent through the whole fire — it only beeps at toast.
They're forecasting hot black snow this weekend — summer's really committing this year.
The new submarine only sails on the surface and can't dive — basically a boat with commitment issues.
My shark dentures regrow on their own — soft teeth, but they keep coming back.
The new camera takes naps instead of photos — great battery life, zero memories.
I eat my cereal dry with soda for dinner — milk is for mornings, which I don't do.
She buttered her toast with a stick of wood — it never melted, which she calls "rustic."
I had breakfast for dinner last night — cereal at midnight, because mornings are just a suggestion.
The thieves tried to steal the steel — they got the metal but left the irony.
I hit the brake so hard I thought something would break — it did, my coffee.
The hotel suite smelled sweet — like someone had baked dessert in the bathtub.
I dropped a cent in the gutter and now it has a scent — Eau de Drain.
I ate the chili on the porch and got chilly — the bowl was the only warm thing out there.
He hummed a tune while eating his tuna — the song of the sea, twice.
The baby wailed like a whale — the neighbors heard the ocean.
My rent is due and all I can offer is the dew on the grass — morning's collateral.
The doe ate my dough — the deer finished the bread and my weekend.
He ate the whole donut, hole included — dedication.
My socks are so holey they've become holy — a miracle of laundry.
The fish sole was so good it touched my soul — dinner and salvation.
That might be a mite — either a possibility or a bug, and I'm hoping for the bug.
The school band got banned — apparently drums count as noise pollution.
Like father, like sun — my son rises at noon and sets at midnight.
